thread.title: How Low Can Apple Stock Go? Analysts Are Slashing Their Price Targets

title: How Low Can Apple Stock Go? Analysts Are Slashing Their Price Targets
text:
How Low Can Apple Stock Go? Analysts Are Slashing Their Price Targets By Jan. 3, 2019 10:20 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Nicolas Asfouri/AFP/Getty Images Text size
Wall Street is turning less optimistic on Apple stock (AAPL) due to the magnitude of the company’s guidance warning for the all-important holiday quarter.
On Wednesday, Apple said it now expects sales of approximately $84 billion for the December quarter versus the Wall Street consensus of $91.3 billion, according to FactSet. On Nov. 1, Apple gave a sales outlook range of $89 billion to $93 billion for the December quarter.
Jefferies analyst Timothy O’Shea lowered his price target for Apple stock to $160 from $225, citing his concerns over future iPhone sales. He also reduced his rating on the shares to Hold from Buy.
“We still think Apple can build a massive Services business over time. But Apple hasn’t missed its guide in years, so the extent of this miss suggests it is navigating uncharted waters,” he wrote on Thursday. “We move to the sidelines and wait for clarity as uncertainty grows around the hardware business.”
Apple’s stock was down 9% to $143.83 in early trading Thursday.
Read more: Apple Blamed China for Falling Revenue, but That’s Just a Convenient Excuse
In similar fashion, BMO Capital Markets analyst Tim Long reduced his price target to $153 from $213 for Apple stock. He reaffirmed his Market Perform rating for the shares.
The “new revenue guidance is dramatically lower than prior expectations based on iPhones,” he wrote on Wednesday. “We have been cautious surround the newly launched iPhone’s ability to drive an upgrade cycle, particularly in China, and December quarter results are worse than we would have expected.”
Apple shares had already declined nearly 30% since the end of October through Wednesday as concerns had mounted about weak demand for the iPhone models released last fall, amid a number of smartphone supplier warnings .
CEO Tim Cook blamed China as the key driver for Apple’s lowered sales guidance. China generated 18% of the company’s sales in its September quarter.
“While we anticipated some challenges in key emerging markets, we did not foresee the magnitude of the economic deceleration, particularly in Greater China,” Cook said in a news release Wednesday.
Despite the weak numbers, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee is bullish on Apple’s long-term future. He reiterated his Overweight rating on the stock, citing its strong services business.
We are “looking past the largely cyclical volume headwinds to focus on the accelerating transformation to Services and leverage of the large installed base driving upside through a combination of earnings growth and potential multiple re-rating,” Chatterjee wrote on Thursday.
Nevertheless, he lowered his price target for Apple stock to $228 from $266.
